items.question: What condition must hold for death to have no power over one whose splendor is immortal?
premises: Death does not arise for that person.
That person possesses imperishable status.
Immortal splendor marks the nature of that person.
items.inference: One endowed with immortal splendor is beyond the reach of death.
items.plain_english: Indeed, death does not come to him; he is imperishable, of immortal splendor.

items.question: Under what affective condition is one said to be capable of shaking the triple world with all its moving and unmoving things?
premises: Anger is the stated condition for action.
The object is the triple world including moving and unmoving things.
The action is one of shaking.
items.inference: When angered, one can shake the entire triple world, moving and unmoving alike.
items.plain_english: When angered, O goddess, one can shake the triple world together with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What determines the nature of an accomplishment attained through practice?
premises: Accomplishment arises in connection with constant practice.
The nature of that accomplishment corresponds to its cause.
No other factor is stated as decisive here.
items.inference: The character of the accomplishment is exactly such as constant practice makes it.
items.plain_english: Such as constant practice is, so too does the accomplishment become.

items.question: What kind of knowledge is identified as supreme in this teaching?
premises: This is knowledge.
That knowledge is supreme.
It is the knowledge of autonomy-accomplishment of mind.
items.inference: The supreme knowledge here is the knowledge that is autonomy-accomplishment of mind.
items.plain_english: This knowledge is supreme; it is the knowledge of autonomy-accomplishment of mind.

items.question: By whom and under what condition is this knowledge to be taken up?
premises: It is to be taken up by effort.
It belongs to the Kaula domain.
It is to be taken up by one who desires accomplishment.
items.inference: One who desires accomplishment must take it up with effort in the Kaula path.
items.plain_english: It is to be taken up with effort in the Kaula path by one who desires accomplishment.

items.question: What sequence of actions is prescribed to fix the mind in that place?
premises: The tongue is to be turned upward.
Having done so, the mind is to be fixed in that place.
Fixation is the intended action.
items.inference: Turning the tongue upward and fixing the mind there is the prescribed practice.
items.plain_english: Having turned the tongue upward, one should fix the mind in that place.

items.question: What is the temporal scope of freedom from illness, death, old age and the like?
premises: Freedom occurs in a moment.
The sources of bondage are illness, death, old age and others.
Freedom is from those sources.
items.inference: In a single moment, one is freed from illness, death, old age and the like.
items.plain_english: In a moment, one is freed from diseases, from illness, death, old age and so on.

items.question: Under what condition is disease destroyed in a moment?
premises: Destruction occurs in a moment.
The condition stated is pungent substance.
The result named is destruction related to leprosy.
items.inference: In a moment, disease is destroyed when in contact with pungent substance as a leprosy-destroying means.
items.plain_english: In a moment, disease is destroyed by pungent substance, which destroys leprosy.

items.question: By what means does a wise man become immortal?
premises: The means is the taste of milk.
The agent is a wise man.
The result is becoming immortal.
items.inference: By means of the taste of milk, a wise man becomes immortal.
items.plain_english: By the taste of milk, a wise man becomes immortal.

items.question: Where and at what moment is the mind to be placed according to this prescription?
premises: The mind is to be placed in the circle in the nose.
It is also to be placed at the time of yawning.
Both placements are prescribed.
items.inference: One should place the mind in the nasal circle and place it at the moment of yawning.
items.plain_english: One should place the mind in the circle of the nose; one should place it at the time of yawning.

items.question: What forms of being may one attain through this practice?
premises: One may become a divine maiden of the gods.
One may also become a yakṣa-vidyādhara.
Both are stated as possible results.
items.inference: Through this practice one may attain the form of a divine maiden of the gods or of a yakṣa-vidyādhara.
items.plain_english: One may become a divine maiden of the gods, and also a yakṣa-vidyādhara.

items.question: What action follows the attraction of many divine maidens?
premises: Many divine maidens are attracted.
Attraction is the prior action.
Those maidens then enjoy.
items.inference: Having attracted many divine maidens, one enjoys with them, O beloved.
items.plain_english: Having attracted many divine maidens, they enjoy with you, O beloved.

items.question: By what means is a yogin said to become one of upward semen, and by what means is he not?
premises: A yogin becomes upward-semen by this practice.
He is not a yogin by the hand.
The distinction is one of means.
items.inference: It is by retention upward, not by manual means, that one becomes a yogin of upward semen.
uncertainties: Surface karata(? is uncertain in reading; morphological assignment is tentative.
items.plain_english: The yogin becomes one of upward semen; he is not a yogin by hand, O beloved.

items.question: What is claimed about the attainability of this circle relative to other yoga?
premises: This circle is difficult to obtain.
There is no yoga higher than this.
Attainability is restricted by its rarity.
items.inference: This circle is difficult to obtain, for there is no yoga higher than it.
items.plain_english: This circle is difficult to obtain; there is no yoga higher than this.

items.question: What result follows from practice when done step by step?
premises: Practice is the domain.
When practiced step by step, it produces a result.
That result is great and wonder-causing.
items.inference: Practice carried out step by step produces something of great wonder.
items.plain_english: In practice, when practiced step by step, it produces great wonder.

items.question: For whom is there no doubt in this matter?
premises: Doubt does not arise here.
The condition is devotion to constant practice.
That condition applies to a specific class.
items.inference: For those devoted to constant practice, there is no doubt here.
items.plain_english: There is no doubt here for those who are devoted to constant practice.

items.question: What result is stated in connection with muttering before an image?
premises: The context is muttering in relation to an image.
A result is stated there.
That result is breaking of pot and stone.
items.inference: In the context of image-muttering, breaking of pot and stone is stated as the result.
uncertainties: Surface tasmi(n is a fused/truncated form as given; internal boundary not expanded per fidelity rules.
items.plain_english: In image-muttering, there is breaking of pot and stone.

items.question: Which deities are named as present in this context?
premises: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Yama and Indra are named.
Varuṇa is named.
Vāyu is named.
items.inference: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Yama, Indra, Varuṇa and Vāyu are named here.
items.plain_english: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Yama and Indra, and Varuṇa and Vāyu too.

items.question: Which classes of beings are listed alongside the deities in this sequence?
premises: Gandharvas are listed.
Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Nāgas and Vidyādharas are listed.
The address is to the beloved.
items.inference: Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Nāgas and Vidyādharas are named here.
items.plain_english: Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Nāgas and Vidyādharas, O beloved.

items.question: What two attributes are ascribed to the object shown in this context?
premises: It is endowed with constellations and stars.
It is encompassed as the universe.
Both attributes are stated together.
items.inference: What is shown is endowed with constellations and stars and is the encompassed universe.
items.plain_english: Endowed with constellations and stars, the universe is encompassed.

items.question: By what means and in how many forms is one's own body shown?
premises: The means is constant meditation.
The object shown is one's own body.
It is shown in many ways.
items.inference: By constant meditation, one's own body is shown in many ways.
items.plain_english: By constant meditation, one may show one's own body in many ways.

items.question: What kind of accomplishment arises from practice, and by what authority?
premises: Accomplishment arises from practice.
It is eightfold.
It is enjoined by scripture.
items.inference: From practice arises an eightfold accomplishment that is enjoined by scripture.
items.plain_english: From practice comes accomplishment, eightfold and enjoined by scripture.

items.question: To whom is this Kaula teaching to be given, and to whom is it not?
premises: This Kaula is to be given to the worthy.
It is not to be given to just anyone.
The restriction is by worthiness.
items.inference: This Kaula teaching is to be given to the worthy, but not to whomever it may be.
items.plain_english: This Kaula is to be given to the worthy; it is not to be given to just anyone.

items.question: What obligation falls to one who is firmly resolved regarding this extraction?
premises: This extraction is to be concealed.
The concealment is to be constant.
It falls to one who is firmly resolved.
items.inference: One who is firmly resolved must always conceal this extraction.
items.plain_english: This extraction is to be always concealed by one who is firmly resolved.
